issue: Information overload — hero number, comparison bars, stat row, and IEA banner all compete for attention; the 20% stat appears three separate times (bars, stat row, hero context).
fix: Remove the stat-row entirely (it repeats the bars). Let the bars carry the historical comparison and the hero number carry the shock magnitude. One repetition, not three.

issue: Title says 'peaked at $156' and 'rupee hit all-time low' but the visual hierarchy buries the rupee (93.29 is a small KPI card). Two claims, one visual anchor.
fix: Either split into two hero numbers side-by-side (dual focal point) or sharpen the title to the single most consequential metric. Add a directional arrow or % change on the rupee KPI to make the FX move visually proportionate to the crude move.

issue: Strong map-message alignment. Minor: the numbered markers (①–④) are arbitrary cluster locations that could mislead a reader into thinking these are verified AIS positions; legend is slightly dense for mobile.
fix: Add a small 'illustrative positioning' disclaimer on the map. Collapse legend into a single row with tighter spacing.

issue: Title buries the lead — 'Crude is manageable' is an unsupported assertion that undercuts urgency. The bar chart only has two bars, making it visually thin for a full-viewport card. The 90% → 20% drop is the real story but isn't the hero visual.
fix: Rewrite title to: 'LPG imports collapsed 80% overnight — 330M households now rationed.' Make a single hero number (–80% or 90→20%) the focal point. Use the bar chart as supporting evidence, not the centrepiece.

issue: Excellent so-what ('diplomacy ≠ reopening'). Minor: the CSS timeline markers crowd on small screens — labels overlap around weeks 0–2.
fix: Increase left-margin on the week-2 marker or stack the date/label vertically with a slight rightward offset. Test at 375px width.

issue: Act break is structurally useful but the so-what is weak — 'Capacity, slate, and supply are no longer yours to control' is atmospheric, not actionable. The three preview chips all say 'Next section covers' which is redundant.
fix: Replace the tagline with a quantified stake: 'Your refinery is running at 65% gas, losing ₹52/litre on diesel, and facing a crude slate you didn't choose.' Drop the 'Next section covers' labels — let the chip titles speak for themselves.

issue: Hero number '100K' is ambiguous — it could be read as total capacity rather than the offline portion. The 'SUSPENDED' export KPI lacks quantification (how much export revenue lost?).
fix: Reframe hero as '–100K bbl/d' with a clear 'of 300K total' subtitle directly adjacent. Add an estimated export revenue loss figure to the SUSPENDED KPI to make the financial consequence concrete.

issue: Chart and title align well (complexity = survival). The RIL annotation label may collide with the bar on narrow screens. The NCI explanation is buried in the insight box — a reader unfamiliar with it won't grasp the mechanism from the chart alone.
fix: Add NCI values as secondary labels on the y-axis (e.g., 'IOCL · NCI 7'). Ensure the annotation label uses xAdjust dynamically or falls back to a tooltip.

issue: The CSS Sankey is creative but the flow logic is confusing — 'Total Gas Supply = 100%' flows to Fertilizer (70%), LPG (MAX), and Refinery (65%), which sums to >100% and conflates allocation priority with volume share. The visual implies additive splits.
fix: Clarify that these are priority tiers, not volume shares — relabel the diagram as a priority cascade (waterfall) rather than a Sankey. Show: Total → LPG (first call) → Fertilizer (70% guaranteed of remainder) → Refinery (residual = 65% of baseline). Make the math traceable.

issue: Stronger than c06 — the three numbered clocks give structure. But 'three separate clocks running down simultaneously' is still abstract. No quantified stakes on this card itself.
fix: Add a single aggregate number: e.g., 'Combined exposure: ₹X lakh crore over 90 days' or a countdown timer to the first binding deadline. Make the reader feel time pressure, not just read about it.

issue: Waterfall chart is the right choice; ₹52/litre gap is visceral and memorable. Minor: the waterfall uses floating bars which Chart.js may render inconsistently; the 'Retail Price' bar starting from 0 breaks waterfall convention (it should be a marker, not a bar).
fix: Replace the retail-price bar with a horizontal annotation line only (you already have one). This keeps the waterfall logic clean: build-up bars → total cost → gap. Removes visual redundancy.

issue: Excellent urgency framing — countdown, timeline, and zero-renewal-signals triplet all reinforce. The title conflates 2025 and 2026 dates (waiver says 2025 but crisis context is 2026), which may confuse careful readers.
fix: Verify and harmonize the year across all date references. If the waiver is indeed 2025 and the crisis is 2026, add a one-line contextual note explaining the temporal relationship.

issue: Good binary framing (talks succeed vs. fail). The chart script is truncated (annotation config cut off), so rendering may break. 'GS OUTLOOK: 3-DIGIT' KPI is vague — it doesn't specify a price or timeframe.
fix: Complete the annotation config. Replace '3-DIGIT' with the actual GS target (e.g., '$110–130 through 2027') to make the KPI falsifiable and credible. Vague KPIs erode trust.
